observedCues.limits: The inspected passage establishes corridor movement only. It does not establish a player-controlled enemy-evasion encounter or a same-enemy narrow/wide comparison. Exclude the scripted reveal from the required motion evidence.

observedCues.first: At file 22–24 seconds Jill and an upright zombie are visible between the near walls. The figure positions shift across the width of the passage.
observedCues.second: At 26–34 seconds the fixed camera switches to an overhead view. Jill changes position and aims along the passage. A figure is visible at its far end in the 34-second sample.
observedCues.result: At 36 and 38 seconds Jill is by the far wall beside a low figure. At 40 seconds she is again visibly aiming at the upright enemy. At 44–46 seconds the enemy is on the floor and Jill changes facing.
observedCues.limits: One released-game encounter with several fixed camera views. No inferred input, damage event, collision measurement, reason for retreat, tested wide-space result or claim of enemy identity across other rooms.

openingCueDraft.ko: 질이 좁은 복도에서 좀비와 마주칩니다. 벽이 가까우면 옆으로 움직일 수 있는 공간부터 줄어들죠. 같은 공격을 두고 벽 간격만 벌리면 피할 길이 어떻게 달라질까요?
openingCueDraft.en: Jill meets a zombie in a narrow hallway. Close walls leave less room to move sideways. If the attack stays the same and only the walls move apart, how does the available escape route change?
openingCueDraft.conformance: Introduce the visible corridor encounter first. Carry the wall and body relation into the authored width-only comparison. Actual footage supplies the phenomenon and the authored model supplies the controlled result. Keep the existing P02–P07 learning order.
